findings.title: idle_timeout validation accepts "0s", which silently disables idle shutdown
findings.explanation: The regex ^[0-9]+s$ accepts "0s". Per the provider schema for google_colab_runtime_template.idle_shutdown_config.idle_timeout: "An input of 0s disables the idle shutdown feature, and a valid range is [10m, 24h]." A consumer passing "0s" gets a runtime that never shuts down - an e2-standard-4 plus a 100GB disk billing indefinitely - with no error from Terraform. The same regex also accepts out-of-range values like "5s" or "999999s", which the API rejects only at apply time.
findings.remediation: Constrain the numeric value to the API's documented [600s, 86400s] window so 0s and out-of-range values fail at plan time with a clear message.

findings.title: disk_type hardcoded to pd-standard while every sibling spec field is parameterised
findings.explanation: machine_type, disk_size_gb, idle_timeout, description and labels are all variables, but disk_type is a literal "pd-standard". pd-standard is HDD-backed; a consumer wanting pd-balanced or pd-ssd for notebook I/O has to fork the module. It is the only inconsistent field in the resource.
findings.remediation: Add a disk_type variable defaulting to "pd-standard" so the current behaviour is unchanged for existing callers.

findings.title: network/subnetwork descriptions say "Self-link" but the working usage passes .id
findings.explanation: Both descriptions read "Self-link of the VPC network/subnetwork". A self_link is the https://www.googleapis.com/... URL; the Colab API wants the projects/{project}/global/networks/{name} form, which is what .id produces. example/examplea/module.colab.tf correctly passes google_compute_network.colab.id, so the documented contract contradicts the only working example. A consumer following the description and passing .self_link gets an apply-time error.
findings.remediation: Reword both descriptions to name the .id form explicitly.
findings.fix: description = "Resource ID of the VPC network the runtime attaches to, e.g. google_compute_network.x.id"

findings.title: kms_key_name marked sensitive though a KMS key resource name is not a secret
findings.explanation: A Cloud KMS key resource name (projects/../locations/../keyRings/../cryptoKeys/..) is an identifier, not key material - it appears in IAM bindings and audit logs. Marking it sensitive redacts it from plan output, making CMEK misconfiguration harder to spot in review, and Terraform propagates sensitivity to any output or expression derived from it.

findings.title: Placeholder non-empty-string validations on location and machine_type
findings.explanation: length(trimspace(x)) > 0 only rejects the empty string. var.location is a GCP region and var.machine_type a GCE machine type; both have well-defined shapes, so a typo like "europe-west-2" or "e2-standard" passes validation and fails at apply.
findings.remediation: Replace with shape-checking regexes: ^[a-z]+-[a-z]+[0-9]$ for location and ^[a-z][0-9]-[a-z]+(-[0-9]+)?$ for machine_type. Verify against the defaults europe-west2 and e2-standard-4 before applying.

findings.title: "europe-west2" repeated as a literal in three example files
findings.explanation: The region literal appears in google_compute_subnetwork.colab (region), google_kms_key_ring.colab (location) and the module call (location). Changing the example's region means editing three files and is easy to do partially - a keyring in the wrong region against a subnet in another is an apply-time failure.
findings.remediation: Introduce a local (locals { region = "europe-west2" }) in the example and reference it from all three.

findings.title: network_tags not exposed, so firewall rules cannot target the runtime
findings.explanation: google_colab_runtime_template supports a network_tags attribute, but the module neither sets nor exposes it. The example defines firewall rules on the VPC that can only be scoped by source CIDR, not by target tag, so a consumer cannot write a rule that applies to the runtime specifically.
findings.remediation: Add an optional network_tags variable (type list(string), default []) and wire it to the resource.

suggested_policies.rationale: google_colab_runtime_template has zero policy coverage in holden today (coverage_by_type reports only wildcard HLD_TF_* rules for it). An idle_timeout of "0s" is the provider's documented way to disable idle shutdown entirely, leaving a Colab Enterprise runtime VM and its persistent disk billing indefinitely. Both the omitted-block and the explicit-0s cases are unambiguous static checks on one attribute path.
suggested_policies.yaml:
id: HLD_GCP_539
name: Colab Enterprise runtime templates must keep idle shutdown enabled
principle: cost
severity: MEDIUM
rationale: |
  A Colab Enterprise runtime holds its machine and persistent disk for as long
  as it is running. The provider documents idle_shutdown_config.idle_timeout as
  accepting "0s" to disable the idle shutdown feature outright, and the valid
  range otherwise as [10m, 24h]. A template with the block omitted, or with
  idle_timeout = "0s", leaves every runtime created from it running until a
  human notices - the single largest avoidable cost in a notebook estate.
remediation: |
  Set an explicit idle timeout inside the documented range:

    resource "google_colab_runtime_template" "main" {
      idle_shutdown_config {
        idle_timeout = "3600s"
      }
    }
resources:
  google_colab_runtime_template:
    path: idle_shutdown_config.idle_timeout
    required: true
    not_equals: "0s"
